PHIX0001.description:
Critical thinking and reasoning are fundamental skills required for rational, evidence-based argumentation. These high order skills are not just necessary for academic studies, but are actively sought by employers seeking prospective employees with strong reasoning and problem solving skills to ensure continuation of operational productivity. Moreover, educators often demand students to construct cohesive, logically structured expositions to test theoretical knowledge; consequently, this unit aims to explicitly teach components of reasoned argumentation. By scrutinising the anatomy of an argument, students will learn to identify elements of reasoning; distinguish characteristics of varying types of arguments; and recognise elements of faulty reasoning.

Application of this knowledge will enable students to produce reasoned argumentation and possess the ability to critically analyse and evaluate credibility of various arguments in discipline specific contexts. Furthermore, within this robust and inquiring environment, students will also develop skills of information processing, problem solving and creative thinking. Finally, the teaching of metacognitive strategies will encourage students to reflect and assess the efficacy of their higher order thinking strategies, a necessary attribute of lifelong learners.
PHIX0001.outcomes:
Students are able to (1) apply knowledge of logic to engage in robust methods of questioning and production of credible argumentation; (2) critically evaluate the validity of argumentation of a variety of written and spoken texts; (3) communicate clear, cohesive and logical argumentation; (4) demonstrate critical thinking and problem-solving skills to address complex issues with

reasoned justification and with a degree of intellectual independence.; and (5) evaluate divergent perspectives and generate new ideas to address complex discipline

related problems in collaborative learning situations..
PHIX0001.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) source analysis; (2) project; and (3) debate. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
